Sunlight looks white but is really made of all the colours of the rainbow. When it passes through the air, the tiny bits of air bounce blue light around much more than red or yellow light. So when you look up, blue light comes at you from every direction and the sky looks blue.
The sky is blue because it reflects the colour of the oceans.
Due to Rayleigh scattering, whose cross-section scales with the inverse fourth power of wavelength, shorter wavelengths dominate the diffuse skylight spectrum.
Sunlight has every colour in it. Air scatters blue light the most. That scattered blue light reaches your eyes from all over the sky. That is why the sky looks blue. At sunset it turns orange.
Light from the sun is a mix of colours. Air bumps blue light around much more than the other colours, so blue fills the whole sky.
